title: Charles E Allen Barbershop. In 1932, haircuts were 25 cents, shave 10 cents
description: Charles E. Allen, a barber, is pictured taking a break in front of his shop on upper Main Street (Building still present). After arriving in Hartland in 1893, he quickly established his barbershop and became a mentor to many, including Ike Hovey and Roy Stevens, who later opened their own shops. In those early days, a haircut cost 15 cents and a shave 10 cents. Outside of work, Allen was passionate about horse racing. He travelled to various events with his chestnut stallion, Calumet Duds, and sold the horse in 1936 when it was six years old. On Sundays, Allen would take out his dappled horse, driving a carriage with his daughter, Edna and his wife seated in the back, while he sat up front in his suit, tie, and felt hat. His wife managed the first Farmers Telephone office above his barber shop.
